documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up. Took his last isoniazid dose Sunday, which makes 9 months. No nausea, jaundice or numbness at any point. No cough or sweats.

Since the hospital: no headaches, working full time again from home, energy normal. Not missing ART doses, pill box and alarm still working. Fluconazole and TMP-SMX daily without problems; no rash.

Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF daily, fluconazole 400 mg daily, TMP-SMX DS daily. Stopping INH and B6 today. NKDA.

Exam: weight up again since November. Well. No thrush, no adenopathy. Heart, lungs normal. Abdomen soft, no spleen. Neuro: normal mentation, cranial nerves, strength, gait.

A/P
1. Latent TB: INH completed. Off INH and pyridoxine. Will keep LTBI, treated, on the problem list.
2. HIV: CMP, CBC, CD4 and VL today, copy to ID.
3. Cryptococcal meningitis on fluconazole 400 mg per ID. Next ID visit in March.
4. Lipids today since he is on ART.
RTC 4-5 months.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Henry, viral load is now undetectable and CD4 is 228, back over 200. Kidney, liver, blood counts and cholesterol all normal. Please keep the TMP-SMX going for now; ID wants a few months of CD4 above 200 before stopping it.

Date of service: 03/19/2024

Doing well. No headache, vision normal. Adherent. Finished isoniazid in January.

Plan: continue bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF, fluconazole 400 mg daily and TMP-SMX DS daily. Recheck CD4 and VL in about 2 months. He mentions a possible long field assignment this summer; asked him to see us and primary care before he goes.
Allergies: NKDA.

OUTSIDE INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC — FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Date of service: 05/28/2024

Leaving in early July for a field posting of several months in rural East Africa. Clinically well.

CD4 266, HIV RNA not detected (third consecutive undetectable).

Plan: continue all three medicines through the trip. We will reassess TMP-SMX and fluconazole when he is back. Will provide a letter for customs listing his medications. Malaria prophylaxis and travel vaccines to be arranged through primary care and his organization; no interaction concern between bictegravir and atovaquone-proguanil. Follow up here on return.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Pre-travel Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34M before a field posting in rural East Africa, leaving 7/3, likely back in spring. Long malaria-season exposure; his organization's travel clinic is handling the country entry vaccines and he has an appointment there next week.

Feels well. No headaches since fall. Weight back near where he was before the meningitis. Adherent to ART, fluconazole and TMP-SMX per his report and the pharmacy fill history.

Data: ID 5/28 CD4 266, VL undetectable.
Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF daily, fluconazole 400 mg daily, TMP-SMX DS daily. NKDA.

Exam: well. No thrush, no adenopathy. Heart, lungs normal. Abdomen soft, no spleen. Neuro normal.

A/P
1. Malaria prevention: had vivax malaria on a prior posting. Atovaquone-proguanil daily, start 2 days before arrival, continue the whole stay and 7 days after. No interaction with his ART per ID. Nets, repellent, long sleeves at dusk. Any fever while there or in the months after return needs a malaria test the same day, and to mention vivax history and HIV.
2. HIV, controlled: enough ART for the first 90 days; pharmacy will request a vacation override; remaining fills by mail to his organization's base. ID customs letter in hand.
3. Cryptococcal meningitis on fluconazole 400 mg; TMP-SMX continues. ID to review both on return.
4. CBC and BMP today on TMP-SMX.
Safe travels. Message through the portal from abroad; see him when he is back.

documents.title: Vacation supply override
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called MassHealth pharmacy line with the pharmacy on a 3-way call. Travel override approved for 90-day supplies of bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF, fluconazole and TMP-SMX. Atovaquone-proguanil filled for the full posting. Pt picked up all four 6/21. CBC and BMP from 6/18 normal; pt notified in portal.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 04/08/2025 via the ED, discharged 04/12/2025

Diagnosis: Plasmodium vivax malaria, uncomplicated, from a chloroquine-sensitive area. Hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia from malaria.
Other: HIV-1 on ART; history of cryptococcal meningitis on fluconazole; latent TB, treated.

History: 35 yo M, aid worker, home three weeks ago from about nine months in rural East Africa. Did not take malaria prophylaxis while there, though he had been prescribed it. Four days of fever, chills, tiredness and a vague ache in the belly. The fevers came every second day with drenching sweats, headache and muscle aches. Had vivax malaria once before on an earlier posting.

On arrival: temperature 39.5 C. Looked tired and a little sweaty. Yellow sclerae. Spleen tip felt 2 cm under the left ribs. No neck stiffness, normal mental status.

Labs: hemoglobin 9.2, platelets 90,000, reticulocytes 4.8%, LDH 340, total bilirubin 2.3. Thick and thin smears: P. vivax, 0.6% parasitemia. G6PD normal.

Course: Oral chloroquine over 3 days; fever broke on hospital day 2, repeat smear on day 3 negative for parasites. Primaquine 30 mg base daily for 14 days started at discharge for radical cure after normal G6PD. ART, fluconazole and TMP-SMX continued. Tolerated food and was walking the halls by discharge.

Home medications on discharge:
- primaquine 30 mg base daily x14 days (NEW)
- bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide daily
- fluconazole 400 mg daily
- TMP-SMX DS daily
- isoniazid 300 mg daily, pyridoxine 50 mg daily (per patient list on file)
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: ID clinic in 4 weeks with CBC; primary care as needed. Return for fever, dark urine or yellowing.

documents.title: Prior authorization renewal
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Annual MassHealth renewal for bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF submitted and approved through 4/2026.

documents.title: Hospital stay
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Heads up, I've been back since mid-March and ended up in the hospital for 4 days with malaria (vivax again). I'm better. They gave me a 2-week pill for the liver stage. I didn't take the prevention pills like I should have, I know. ID is seeing me next month. Do I need to come in too?

documents.title: RE: Hospital stay
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you're through it. We got the hospital summary. Finish all 14 days of the primaquine. ID will check your counts. I'd still like to see you this spring to catch up on everything since last June; the front desk can book a time that works.

documents.title: RE: RE: Hospital stay
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ok. I'll call once I know my work schedule.

documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
OUTSIDE INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC — FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Date of service: 05/20/2025

Seen after his April admission for P. vivax malaria. Completed chloroquine and 14 days of primaquine. No fevers since discharge. Energy improving.

Hemoglobin 12.6, platelets 224. CD4 284, HIV RNA not detected. He reports taking ART daily throughout the posting.

Plan: continue ART, fluconazole and TMP-SMX for now; discuss stopping TMP-SMX at the next visit if CD4 stays above 200. Back in 3 months. Urged primary care follow-up.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 04/11/2026 via the ED to the medical ICU, transferred to medicine 04/14, discharged 04/29/2026

Diagnosis: relapsed cryptococcal meningitis (C. neoformans) with raised opening pressure, in advanced HIV off ART.
Other: HIV-1, CD4 45, viral load 162,000; medication nonadherence; P. vivax malaria treated 2025; latent TB, treated.

History: 36 yo M back in the ED with two weeks of low-grade fevers, headache and feeling unwell, slowly worse. Cryptococcal meningitis in 2023. He says he stopped taking his HIV medicine about six months ago and has not been to ID clinic.

On arrival: T 38.2 C, BP 120/75, HR 88, RR 16. Neck stiff, Brudzinski sign positive. Fundi normal. Cranial nerves, strength and sensation intact; no focal deficit.

CSF on admission: opening pressure 280 mm H2O. WBC 20/uL, 80% lymphocytes. Protein 50 mg/dL. Glucose 25 mg/dL with serum glucose 90. India ink negative. Cryptococcal antigen sent; returned positive at 1:256 the next day. Fungal culture grew C. neoformans on day 6.
CD4 45. HIV RNA 162,000.

Course: ICU for neuro checks and daily therapeutic lumbar punctures until the opening pressure came down to normal by day 5. Reinduction with liposomal amphotericin B and flucytosine for 14 days; electrolytes repleted, kidney function and counts stayed acceptable. Headache resolved, afebrile from day 4. ART deliberately held during induction to lower IRIS risk, with a plan to restart at 4 to 6 weeks in ID clinic. Seen by social work and the HIV adherence team.

Discharge medications:
- fluconazole 800 mg by mouth daily (consolidation, CHANGED from 400 mg)
- TMP-SMX DS 1 tab daily (resume)
- bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide: on hold, ID to restart
- isoniazid 300 mg, pyridoxine 50 mg: listed by prior records, not taking; not resumed
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: ID clinic 2 weeks; primary care. Return for headache, vision change, confusion or fever.

documents.title: Admission notification
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Regional medical center ICU social worker called: pt admitted Saturday, recurrent meningitis, in the ICU. Asked for PCP contact and med list. Fax sent with our last med list and 2024 notes. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Discharge summary reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Discharge summary from the April admission received and reviewed. Relapsed cryptococcal meningitis after months off ART; reinduction done, fluconazole 800 mg consolidation, ART to restart with ID. Their med list still carries isoniazid and B6 from old records. Has not been seen here since 6/2024. Asked front desk to reach out to book a visit after his ID restart.

documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called pt to book a follow-up. Left message. Portal message sent with the scheduling line.

documents.title: Infectious Disease follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
OUTSIDE INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC — FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Date of service: 05/27/2026

Seen after discharge for relapsed cryptococcal meningitis. Also saw him 05/19, when bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide was restarted, 5 weeks after induction began.

Headache gone. No fever. Says he is taking ART and fluconazole every day; using a blister pack from the pharmacy. Had a hard stretch last fall and stopped everything; he is open about it and has accepted a case manager.

Exam: alert, normal mental status, no meningismus, no focal findings.
BMP and CBC today normal.

Plan:
1. Fluconazole 800 mg daily to complete 8 weeks of consolidation, then 200 mg daily maintenance.
2. ART: continue; watch for IRIS (new headache or fever should prompt a call).
3. TMP-SMX DS daily.
4. Return in 8 weeks with CD4 and VL.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Infectious Disease follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
OUTSIDE INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC — FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Date of service: 07/28/2026

Ten weeks back on ART. No headache, fever or vision change; no IRIS features. Case manager visiting weekly. Pharmacy fills on time.

CD4 88, HIV RNA 410 (from 162,000). CMP, CBC normal.

Plan:
1. Consolidation complete; fluconazole now 200 mg daily maintenance, at least 12 months and until CD4 is above 100 with a suppressed viral load for 3 months.
2. Continue bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF and TMP-SMX DS daily.
3. Return in 3 months with CD4 and VL.
We have asked him to reconnect with primary care.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: ID letter filed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ID 7/28 letter received. Viral load down to 410, CD4 88, fluconazole now 200 mg. Filed. Still no visit booked here; front desk to try him again.
